notes: Site (templeandwebster.com.au) blocked HTTP fetch (curl_cffi, 5 impersonation profiles) and Playwright/Chromium headless (with stealth args) with a Cloudflare managed challenge -- both tiers returned 'Just a moment...' consistently, matching the prior-pass note. Found a genuine site-wide 'New Arrivals' PLP via a homepage banner tile (https://www.templeandwebster.com.au/New-Arrivals-C1814756.html, distinct from a Furniture-scoped 'New Furniture' link that also exists inside the Furniture nav dropdown -- the banner tile is the canonical, undifferentiated listing). The New Arrivals page is a real PLP: product grid, filters, sort options including a dedicated 'New Arrivals' sort, '489 Results' header. It also exposes genuine per-department children (site's own relatedLink data + on-page sub-nav for New Furniture/New Rugs/New Decor/etc.), each with its own URL and its own exact count fetched the same way -- kept as leaf rows under the New Arrivals parent, mirroring the shared engine's grouping pattern. Sum of the 13 children (522) exceeds the parent total (489) -- expected: a product can be tagged into more than one department facet (e.g. an item that is both Bed & Bath and Decor), so per-department New Arrivals rollups double-count relative to the deduplicated site-wide listing. This is not a data error; both counts are the site's own exact numbers, verified via each page's '<N> Results' header text. No other New Arrivals-style page (New In, Just Arrived, Latest, What's New) was found in main nav, footer, or department pages; the department pages' own sort dropdowns include 'New Arrivals' as a sort order, which is expected and not a separate PLP.
